acceptance_gate: A proves when a twist is well defined for a fair contact with three hidden places, that independent fair polarities hide it, that two-hidden contacts give pair-worlds, when the monotone world can contradict, and that in worlds with a planar universal satisfier every minimal contradiction winds; B decides under a frozen contract, with an independent checker, which complement-closed contacts on triangular tori contradict locally, never, or only through the twist, and whether winding contradiction events can be measured.
objective: The owner asked for a cheap feasibility check of the three-literal side: reread the contact-census and base-three results, try to define a twisted three-literal world where the twist matters, and see whether a lone-contradiction event can be defined, keeping a quick failure as a useful negative. The census contacts (two hidden joints and one visible fair spoke) give pair-worlds once the spoke is fixed, so a genuinely three-literal hidden world needs three hidden places per contact. With independent fair polarities a twist is invisible. Scoping (scratch, not evidence): the twist is well defined exactly for contacts whose two relations are swapped by flipping every literal; the monotone contact from four-place not-all-equal never contradicts on triangular tori in any twist (a twisted not-all-equal colouring always exists); and among the complement-closed contacts some never contradict on planar patches yet contradict on tori in every twist but one, so every contradiction there must wind. A: the definitions and the structural lemmas, proved. B: the census on fresh tori, frozen, with the winding of minimal contradictions measured.
status: Complete 2026-10-23. Feasibility check positive. Proved: for fair contacts with a visible bit and three hidden places a twist is a cohomology class exactly when the contact is complement-closed (otherwise a contractible seam is a defect); independent fair polarities hide every twist; the monotone world from four-place not-all-equal never contradicts on triangular tori with sides 2 to 5 (frozen); when the doubly allowed patterns tile the plane, planar patches and fitting twists never contradict and every minimal contradiction winds, along classes on which the twist differs from every fitting twist. Census (frozen experiment): of 120 complement-closed placements, 66 contradict locally and 54 tile; for 30 three-place tiling placements the twist decides contradiction; all 7481 minimal contradictions wind (5150 lines, 2331 crosses), and lines run along classes the relative twist makes odd. A first statement of the monotone world's colourings was false on four two-row tori and is corrected. Recommendation: Continue with the dual-pair identity for three-place line contradictions; interest 2/3; deferred to the owner.
stop_rule: One bounded feasibility epic. Stop when A is proved and B has classified the contacts under its frozen rule; the analogues of walls and shielding for winding contradictions are left to a later epic.
title: Twisted three-literal worlds: where the twist decides contradiction
